(1) structure validation is an important step in the structural biology process that can help identify problems with the structure, (2) structure validation methods have improved significantly in recent years, (3) structure validation can help identify structures with problems, but it cannot replace careful inspection by a knowledgeable scientist, and (4) structure validation can be improved by the use of more advanced methods, such as the use of NCS and computational models in molecular replacement
the quality of structures deposited in the PDB is generally good, but that the quality of the data is highly dependent on the quality of the structure.

the quality of structures from structural biology can be improved by using a combination of structure validation and rebuilding, and that the use of structure validation is essential in the development of automated methods for structure determination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality control of structural models,
the development of new tools and protocols for structural validation and the improvement of existing methods.
improving the quality of structural biology data by applying a combination of automated and manual methods to validate and rebuild structural models.

the quality of structures deposited in the PDB is highly variable.
the current state-of-the-art validation methods are sufficient to detect the majority of the errors in structural models, but that there are still some errors that remain difficult to detect.
the PDB is an excellent resource for macromolecular structure data and that it is improving in terms of the quality of the data deposited.

structure validation is a critical component of structural biology, and the development of new methods and protocols is needed to improve the quality of structures deposited in the PDB.
